readout: Lipid phosphatase activity in a humanised yeast assay, where PTEN function is required to prevent phosphoinositide accumulation and so to permit growth; higher is more active
assay_method: Massively parallel functional testing of PTEN in a humanised yeast model. Variant libraries were built by tiling inverse PCR, close to the mutagenesis-integrated-tiles approach, recombined into plasmids by SLiCE, and pooled to give saturation coverage of each quadrant of PTEN. Selection was p110-alpha-CAAX-mediated, with two biological replicates each carrying three technical replicate selections, and sequencing was paired-end 300 bp on Illumina MiSeq. Per-variant scores were taken from the authors' MaveDB deposit.
remark: The sequence is UniProt P60484 exactly, 403 aa, and every label verifies against it. Of the deposit's 8681 rows, 7260 scored substitutions are kept. All 403 single-residue deletion rows are dropped: an indel has no {WT}{position}{MUT} form, so the four-column format cannot express one. All 403 nonsense rows are dropped, a premature stop not being writable as a substitution. 397 substitutions and all 217 synonymous rows carry no score and go too. The wild-type row is the deposit's own _wt entry and reads exactly 1, the score being defined against wild type. The deposit also ships a High_conf flag and per-replicate columns for two biological and six technical replicates; the shipped readout is its combined score, used as it stands, with no confidence filter applied.
